mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to lower cost of capital.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 0.1% and 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate exceeding 4.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, which causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous federal funds rate increases above 4.5% and unemployment rate declines below 4.0% indicate late-cycle monetary tightening in a strong labor market, compressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and UNRATE < 4.0% occur and 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 8.0% during economic slowdowns signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: During economic slowdowns, UNRATE > 8.0% and 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 8.0%) consistently indicates weak labor market conditions, suppressing consumer demand and corporate profit growth, which generates negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 8.0% and 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 600 thousand units (HOUST < 600) indicate weak consumer demand, reducing corporate revenue growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST < 600 and 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, retail sales exceeding 400,000 million dollars (RSAFS > 400,000) signal robust consumer spending, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, RSAFS > 400,000 and 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 90 (INDPRO < 90) indicates weakening economic output, reducing corporate profit growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 90 and 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of such periods.
